Erika Lemay

Show Creator | Sky Dancer | Health Ambassador | Author

Erika Lemay has turned the impossible into her signature—an artist who makes gravity itself look optional. From a four-year-old ballerina to a world-celebrated performer and creator of Physical Poetry , her work has reached hundreds of millions worldwide and earned recognition from Vanity Fair to Le Figaro . Named the “New Queen of Circus” and immortalised by Douglas Kirkland , she has since achieved a Guinness World Record , a historic unanimous Golden Buzzer on America’s Got Talent: Extreme , and appearances on the world’s most prestigious stages. Today, after decades of life-defying performances, she devotes herself to creation as a director—crafting large-scale productions that carry her unique artistic language and redefining what live performance can be. Her book Almost Perfect and her health brand LEMAlab ® extend this vision, reflecting the same pursuit of beauty, discipline, and daring that has made her not only a pioneer, but one of the defining innovators of her generation.

url_citation.content:
This stage of my creative life is intensely stimulating; being a director lets me express the larger canvas I carry in my head.

If you weren’t performing and creating Physical Poetry, what do you imagine yourself doing? Something equally daring – perhaps defying the laws of physics in another way?

I’ve never had an answer to this question. That’s a subject I have deeply explored in my book Almost Perfect , and I long thought I had found my passion very early on, and somehow it was a blessing, but I now know I am inherently passionate and could have been lit up by several career paths. What pulls me is challenge, adrenaline and innovation. The physicality of things is without any doubt a leading force, but the sky is the limit, really. When I left the circus at 19 and started my own venture, there was no path for me to follow, not many international freelance artists in this field and all to be built and traced, I think it’s part of the thrill of it.
If I were not creating for Physical Poetry, I would still chase awe.

...

The closest reference I have is a first kiss with the love of your life: time slows, senses sharpen, and the world briefly organises itself around a single, undeniable now.
